title: Ruth Bowen's license, gangsters and missing contracts
summary: Thomas explains how Joe Glaser helped Bowen get licensed, and her mistakes with gangsters and no contracts.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: But she didn't get the... Did she get the license before Dinah died?
There was Queen Booking, that Dinah wasn't... How did Ruth Bowen have the license?
Well, Ruth Bowen was her manager. She was her manager...
Yeah. So she got involved in starting an agency. And Joe Glaser was instrumental in getting her the license. Because all she had to do was...
She had to give a hundred dollars to the union...

Yeah. Her husband was a musician, but she wasn't no musician. But Joe was instrumental, I think. Because I told her to call Joe, and Joe would help her get a license, show her how to do it. And that's how she got a license to book. And then she got the office at 1650.

And she made one mistake. She got involved with the gangsters. And then another big mistake she made, she didn't get the contracts. And you've got to have contracts. If you don't have a contract on somebody, you know, you ain't got no control over them. And then she was spending money that wasn't hers...
Like who? Like a contract on who did she have to...
Well, she got ahold of a lot of the Rock-and-Roll groups, the singers and whatnot. But then...
All you have to do is give them a contract and they'd have signed it, wouldn't they?

Yeah, they would have signed it. But she didn't have that knowledge. She just believed in freelancing and booking whoever she could. And then she got hold of Aretha Franklin. But Aretha Franklin was kind of... She was on liquor; she drank too much.
